## Keystones

Three, and the new one is independent of the two carried forward.

### K1 — Issue #639, the policy model (ADR 0009)

Dependants: #603, #604, #609, #680, #687, #691, #706, #720, and PRs #692, #675, #684, #671, #638.

Unchanged from the last run except that it has gained a dependant: #720 asks for a `pi --yolo` launcher flag, which is the same configuration-surface question PR #671 answers with a config key.
Five contributor PRs are now parked behind this decision, and the count only grows.

### K2 — Issue #686, the enforcement substrate

Dependants: #609, #680, #698, #706, #713.

Live, and now with a maintainer reply on record (2026-08-10) asking the reporter what attracts them to `nono` and what else they have used.
The tax it measures is unchanged: #694 was fixed and released this week as the fourth escape of the same class (#350, #481, #653, #694), and #713 is a fifth report that the wrapper surface cannot show what actually runs.
The escape cadence did not slow.

### K3 — the prompt-presentation contract (issue not yet filed)

Dependants: #710, #713, #648, #654, and PRs #656, #716.

Four items and two PRs now change how a permission prompt presents itself, and the two PRs edit the same functions in opposite directions: #656 hard-truncates the assembled message to 200 characters, while #716 expands it into aligned `key : value` lines with pretty-printed JSON.
Issue #710 wants it bounded in *height*, which neither addresses.
Reviewing these one at a time guarantees an inconsistent prompt surface, so the contract — what a prompt must always show, what may be elided, and what bounds its size — is the decision to make first.

File it before ranking #656 or #716 on merit.

## Findings that changed a rank

- **#719's misleading denial is verified on `main`.**
  `pollForForwardedResponse` returns `{ approved: false, state: "denied" }` on timeout with no `denialReason` (`packages/pi-permission-system/src/authority/approval-escalator.ts:300-313`), and `denial-messages.ts:228` renders that as `User denied bash command '…'`.
  The stall itself is not yet root-caused: the parent only drains its inbox on a `setInterval` started when `ctx.hasUI` and the context is not a subagent (`forwarding-manager.ts:38-56`), so a parent that never qualifies never answers.
  The reporter is on pi-permission-system 22.0.0 against a current 25.0.0, so the version question comes before the fix.
- **#709 is structurally verified.**
  `SubagentSession.dispose()` calls `this._session.dispose?.()` and emits its own `disposed` event (`packages/pi-subagents/src/lifecycle/subagent-session.ts:194-198`); Pi's `session_shutdown` is emitted by `AgentSessionRuntime.dispose()`, which pi-subagents bypasses.
  The reporter's process accounting matches that gap exactly.
- **#710 is structurally verified.**
  `fitToWidth` wraps long lines rather than clipping them, by explicit design ("so no content is lost", `permission-prompt-component.ts:314-326`), and nothing bounds the resulting row count.
  A large tool input therefore consumes unbounded vertical space.
- **#712 is verified in two places.**
  The wrapper floor rewrites an allow to `{ state: "ask", matchedPattern: WRAPPER_SENTINEL[...] }` while preserving `origin` (`handlers/gates/bash-command.ts:89-90`), and the yolo fast path requires `check.state === "allow"` (`handlers/gates/runner.ts:112`).
  A yolo-origin ask can never take the fast path.
- **#656's premise is stale — this dropped it from rank 5 to 19.**
  The over-wide-line TUI crash was fixed by `e3c69070` on 2026-07-13, released in pi-permission-system v20.7.1, twelve days before the PR was opened on 2026-07-25.
  The PR's remedy also now conflicts with the shipped one: `fitToWidth` deliberately wraps to preserve content, and the PR truncates the assembled message to 200 characters instead.
  Ask the reporter which version they hit the crash on before treating this as a fix.
- **#708 deserves our own investigation, and part of the answer is already in.**
  The published tarballs are clean — `pnpm view @gotgenes/pi-permission-system@latest` reports concrete semver ranges, because `pnpm publish` rewrites `catalog:` specifiers — so `pi install npm:@gotgenes/...` is unaffected.
  What fails is `pi install git:` against this repo, where an npm-based installer meets the `catalog:` entries in every workspace manifest.
  The reporter can no longer reproduce after switching to pnpm, but the git-install path is still broken and it is our manifests it breaks on.
- **Two fresh CI results, both contributor-fixable.**
  PR #716's earlier approved run failed on three Biome errors; the contributor pushed fixes, and the run approved this triage now fails on two `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` errors.
  PR #702 now fails on a single `@typescript-eslint/unified-signatures` error.
  Neither is a design objection; both need a change-request comment from `/pr-review`.
- **The green PRs are still green, and the greens are not stale.**
  #697, #693, #703, #671, and #684 all ran between 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-05, and none of the source files they touch has changed since (latest is 2026-07-27).
  The v25.0.0 breaking change landed in `access-intent/` and `expand-home.ts`, which none of them touch.
- **#684's green is still not an endorsement.**
  It widens who may approve `external_directory` access, and CI has no opinion about a widened security boundary.
- **No cross-package flake surfaced this run.**
  Every `push` run on `main` since 2026-08-05 is green, and no fork PR failed on an unrelated package.

## CI and security audit
